proofs.proof_tex:
Put
\[
u=(\lambda_D,\omega_B,\omega_{\mathrm{diag}})
\quad\text{and}\quad
N=|D|+|B|+n,
\]
so that \(L=\mathbb C(u_1,\ldots,u_N)\). Choose a topological ordering of the acyclic directed graph. In that ordering \(\Lambda^n=0\), and therefore
\[
(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}=I_n+\Lambda+\cdots+\Lambda^{n-1}.
\]
Thus each distinct covariance entry
\[
s_{ij}(u)=\phi_G(\sigma_{ij})
=\bigl[(I_n-\Lambda)^{-\mathsf T}\Omega(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}\bigr]_{ij}
\]
is a polynomial of total degree at most \(2n-1\), represented by an arithmetic circuit of size polynomial in \(n\). Let \(s=(s_{ij}:i\leq j)\), let \(J_0=\partial s/\partial u\), and let \(J_1\) be obtained from \(J_0\) by adjoining the row \(\partial\lambda_e/\partial u\). All entries of these matrices have degree at most \(2n-2\).

We first prove the field-theoretic rank criterion used by the algorithm. Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\in L\), and choose a transcendence basis \(b_1,\ldots,b_r\) of \(\mathbb C(a_1,\ldots,a_m)/\mathbb C\) from among a maximal algebraically independent subfamily of the \(a_i\). Extend it to a transcendence basis \(b_1,\ldots,b_r,c_1,\ldots,c_q\) of \(L/\mathbb C\). The extension
\[
L/\mathbb C(b_1,\ldots,b_r,c_1,\ldots,c_q)
\]
is algebraic and separable because the characteristic is zero. The coordinate derivations with respect to the \(b_j\) extend uniquely through a separable algebraic extension: if \(v\) has minimal polynomial \(g\), differentiating \(g(v)=0\) gives
\[
g'(v)\,dv=-\sum_{ell}v^\ell\,d g_\ell,
\]
and \(g'(v)\neq0\). Applying these extended derivations to a relation \(\sum_j q_j,db_j=0\), with \(q_j\in L\), gives \(q_j=0\) for each \(j\). Hence \(db_1,\ldots,db_r\) are linearly independent over \(L\). Conversely, each \(a_i\) is algebraic over \(\mathbb C(b_1,\ldots,b_r)\); differentiating its separable minimal polynomial expresses \(da_i\) in the \(L\)-span of \(db_1,\ldots,db_r\). Consequently
\[
\dim_L\operatorname{span}_L\{da_1,\ldots,da_m\}
=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C(a_1,\ldots,a_m).
\]

Apply this identity first to the covariance polynomials and then to the covariance polynomials together with \(\lambda_e\). Since the rows of their Jacobians are the coordinate vectors of the corresponding differentials in the basis \(du_1,\ldots,du_N\),
\[
\operatorname{rank}_L J_0=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}K_G,
\qquad
\operatorname{rank}_L J_1=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}K_G(\lambda_e).
\]
Adjoining one element raises transcendence degree by either zero or one. Therefore
\[
\operatorname{rank}_LJ_1=\operatorname{rank}_LJ_0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\lambda_e\text{ is algebraic over }K_G,
\]
whereas a rank increase by one is equivalent to transcendence.

The two generic ranks are obtained by evaluating \(J_0\) and \(J_1\) at one random source point and performing exact Gaussian elimination. Both matrices have at most \(N+1\leq n^2+1\) rows or columns. A nonzero maximal minor has total degree at most
\[
(n^2+1)(2n-2)\leq 2n^3.
\]
Choose the source coordinates independently and uniformly from a finite subset of \(\mathbb Q\) of cardinality at least \(8n^3/\delta\). An evaluated rank can never exceed the generic rank. If it is smaller, a fixed nonzero maximal minor vanished at the chosen point. By \(\mathrm{lem:schwartz\mbox{-}zippel\mbox{-}bound}\), this has probability at most \(\delta/4\) for each of \(J_0\) and \(J_1\). Allowing the remaining \(\delta/2\) budget for the source identity tests recorded in the transcript and applying the union bound gives total symbolic error at most \(\delta\). On the complementary event, equality or a one-rank increase gives the correct tag by the displayed rank criterion. The exact evaluation point, pivot positions, and pivot minors form \(\mathcal J_{G,e}\).

Suppose that the augmented rank is larger. Then \(\lambda_e\) is transcendental over \(K_G\), so the homomorphism
\[
K_G[t]\longrightarrow A_K,
\qquad t\longmapsto\lambda_e,
\]
is injective. Because \(A_K\) is integral by \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\), the induced morphism \(\operatorname{Spec}(A_K)\to\mathbb A^1_{K_G}\) is dominant. Its domain has positive relative dimension, since its fraction field \(L\) contains an element transcendental over \(K_G\). The nonzero augmented pivot minor together with the two rank transcripts is therefore the claimed source-parametric dominance certificate \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\).

On the equality branch, \(d_e(G)<\infty\), and the already established \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\) gives
\[
d_e(G)\leq2^{|D|-n+2}\leq2^{k+1}.
\]
It supplies an upper bound only; no multiplication algebra or eliminant has been constructed.

The nilpotent matrix sum, circuit differentiation, exact evaluations, and Gaussian eliminations use a number of arithmetic operations and transcript entries polynomial in \(n\); the random sampling needs \(O(\log(1/\delta)+\log n)\) bits per coordinate, whose bit cost is charged separately in \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\). Since \(n\geq2\) and \(k\geq0\), a fixed polynomial in \(n\) is bounded by \(n^{C(k+1)}\) for a universal \(C\). This proves the stated time, length, and error guarantees, as well as the explicit absence of \(p_e\)-dependent outputs on the algebraic tag.

added_lemmas.statement: Over a field of characteristic zero, a polynomial system given by straight-line programs and satisfying the reduced regular-sequence hypothesis away from a supplied inequation admits a probabilistic Gröbner-free geometric-resolution algorithm. On successful generic choices, the algorithm represents the relevant zero-dimensional section by a primitive element, its monic polynomial, and rational coordinate parametrizations, with arithmetic complexity polynomial in the straight-line-program evaluation length and the geometric degrees of the successive varieties.

source.locator: main geometric-resolution complexity theorem and the reduced regular-sequence hypothesis

attestation.note: The theorem scope, regularity hypothesis, geometric-resolution output, and polynomial dependence on evaluation length and geometric degree were checked against the cited article; no verbatim wording is reproduced.

added_lemmas.statement: Over a field of characteristic zero, there is a probabilistic lifting-fiber algorithm which, for arbitrary polynomial equations \(f_1=\cdots=f_s=0\) and an inequation \(g\neq0\) given by a straight-line program, computes the equidimensional decomposition of the Zariski closure of their solution set. On successful generic choices the components are encoded by lifting fibers, and the arithmetic complexity is polynomial in the straight-line-program length and the intermediate geometric-degree parameter appearing in the theorem.

attestation.note: The theorem was checked for its characteristic-zero input, equations-and-inequation scope, lifting-fiber output, probabilistic success qualification, and dependence on straight-line-program length and intermediate geometric degree.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\) satisfy \(d_e(G)<\infty\), and suppose a valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\) is supplied for every source-consistent recorded stratum. There is a universal \(a>0\) such that a randomized localized geometric-resolution algorithm returns exactly \((d_e(G),p_e,\mathcal Q_{G,e},h_{G,e})\) with symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\). Its arithmetic construction time and certificate length are at most
\[
(n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^a\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta)),
\]
where \(s=s(\mathfrak C_{G,e})\) and \(\mathfrak d=\mathfrak d(\mathfrak C_{G,e})\). In particular, for any fixed \(b>0\), if \(s\leq n^b\) and \(\mathfrak d\leq n^{b(k+1)}\), then the bound is \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\) for a universal \(C\) depending only on \(a\) and \(b\). The output polynomial is the monic minimal polynomial over \(K_G\), not a whole-fiber eliminant, and \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\) contains the covariance-localization, incidence-lifting, pole, projective-infinity, specialized-leading-coefficient, squarefreeness, and real-lifting circuits whose nonzero product is \(h_{G,e}\). The theorem is conditional on the supplied charts; it does not construct or select them.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a source-consistent recorded stratum and use the notation in \(\mathrm{def:source\mbox{-}prime\mbox{-}chart}\). Validity gives
\[
P K_G[x]_{H\Delta}=(h_1,\ldots,h_c)K_G[x]_{H\Delta},
\qquad
\xi(H\Delta)\neq0.
\]
Thus the localized equations define exactly the source prime on the indicated principal open set, rather than an extensional union containing unidentified components. Because the sequence is reduced and regular and \(\Delta\) is nonzero at the source generic point, the Jacobian criterion makes this open set smooth of pure dimension
\[
q=r-c\leq2k.
\]
Adjoining a variable \(z\) and the equation \(zH\Delta-1=0\) converts the inequation to an equation without changing this principal open set.

Over \(\overline{K_G}\), the finitely many conjugates of \(\lambda_e\) are the roots of its separable minimal polynomial, since the characteristic is zero. Each embedding of \(K_G(\lambda_e)\) into \(\overline{K_G}\) extends to a geometric component of the base change of the source prime. The element \(H\Delta\), being nonzero in that prime and defined over \(K_G\), is nonzero on every conjugate component. For any one such component, the affine hyperplanes that meet it properly and nontrivially form a nonempty Zariski-open set. Intersecting these finitely many open sets and applying \(q\) successive hyperplane sections gives affine linear forms \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_q\) for which the localized slice is nonempty and zero-dimensional on every conjugate component. Transversality is also open, so the choices may be made so that the sliced algebra is reduced.

The hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem:groebner\mbox{-}free\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\) now hold for each chart slice. Its geometric-resolution algorithm produces a finite reduced \(K_G\)-algebra \(B\), multiplication matrices for the exposed coordinates, and the supplied lifting circuits recover every eliminated directed coordinate and the query. Let \(M_e\) be multiplication by \(\lambda_e\) in \(B\), and let
\[
\chi_e(t)=\det(tI-M_e).
\]
Every geometric point of \(B\) lies on the base change of the source prime, hence its queried coordinate is a conjugate of \(\lambda_e\). Conversely, the simultaneous choice of slices meets every conjugate component, so every root of \(p_e\) occurs among the eigenvalues of \(M_e\). Therefore the squarefree part of \(\chi_e\) has exactly the roots of \(p_e\). Both are monic and \(p_e\) is separable, whence
\[
p_e(t)=\operatorname{sqfree}(\chi_e(t)),
\qquad
d_e(G)=\deg p_e.
\]
This equality is the coordinate-projection step: multiplicities and the cardinality of the sliced full fiber do not enter the reported degree.

All coefficients of the chart, multiplication matrices, and lifting maps are elements of \(K_G\) represented by rational covariance circuits. Determinants, greatest common divisors with derivatives, and monic normalization therefore produce coefficientwise rational circuits for \(p_e\). The equality of the localized chart with the source prime ensures that no factor from another incidence component enters \(\chi_e\); source-parametric identity tests certify every zero identity and every proposed nonzero factor. Homogenizing before slicing records the leading forms whose vanishing would create a point at projective infinity. Clearing each rational lifting formula records its pole and incidence-lifting factors. The leading coefficient of the specialized eliminant and its discriminant or squarefreeness resultant are again finite rational covariance circuits. By \(\mathrm{lem:effective\mbox{-}real\mbox{-}quantifier\mbox{-}elimination}\), the existential predicate that a real root extends through the original supported residual equations has an equivalent finite Boolean combination of polynomial sign conditions; by \(\mathrm{lem:real\mbox{-}algebraic\mbox{-}sampling}\), the required exact univariate representations and component sample points can be produced after an algebraic specialization. The elimination and sign polynomials occurring in these two constructions are the real-lifting circuits. Collecting all these factors gives \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), and removing repeated nonzero factors from their product gives a nonzero \(h_{G,e}\). The established incidence-localization theorem ensures that these bookkeeping operations do not invert an undeclared directed-coordinate expression.

The arbitrary-equation and inequation machinery in \(\mathrm{lem:lifting\mbox{-}fiber\mbox{-}equidimensional\mbox{-}decomposition}\) bounds the lifting-fiber operations for the recorded strata, while the reduced-chart solver controls each regular slice. By their cited complexity bounds, multiplication-matrix linear algebra, and the fact that every chart has at most \(2k\) exposed variables, there is a universal \(a>0\) for which the total number of arithmetic operations and output gates is at most
\[
(n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^a\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta)).
\]
Every randomized choice is tested by a displayed nonzero chart, transversality, leading-form, or resultant circuit. Allocating the error budget across the finitely many calls and applying \(\mathrm{lem:schwartz\mbox{-}zippel\mbox{-}bound}\) gives total symbolic error at most \(\delta\).

If \(s\leq n^b\) and \(\mathfrak d\leq n^{b(k+1)}\), then, after increasing constants to cover \(n\geq2\),
\[
(n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^a
\leq n^{2ab(k+1)+a(k+1)}
\leq n^{C(k+1)}
\]
for a constant \(C\) depending only on \(a,b\). This is the asserted fixed-parameter corollary.

The cited algorithms do not remove the antecedent. The Gröbner-free algorithm assumes a reduced regular sequence off an inequation. The lifting-fiber algorithm accepts arbitrary equations and inequations, but outputs all relevant equidimensional components and charges the possibly unbounded intermediate geometric degree. Neither marks which component is the embedded source prime, constructs a source-nonzero Jacobian minor for it, or descends an implicitly presented component to bounded rational circuits over \(K_G\). Source identity testing verifies a proposed chart but does not manufacture one. Hence the conclusion proved here is conditional exactly as stated.
added_lemmas.justification: A bounded reduced chart of the source prime is sufficient to turn the extensional quadratic core into an exact coordinate eliminant and auditable specialization certificate.
added_lemmas.gap: The cited geometric-resolution algorithms solve supplied regular charts or decompose arbitrary systems with intermediate-degree cost; neither selects the embedded source prime or produces its bounded descent over the implicit covariance field.
added_lemmas.consumer: A higher-degree extension of fasttreeid can emit exact degrees and branch polynomials only when the source-prime chart antecedent is certified.

added_lemmas.statement: Does there exist, in \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\), a chart-free randomized algorithm which, for every \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\) with \(d_e(G)<\infty\), constructs the exact tuple \((d_e(G),p_e,\mathcal Q_{G,e},h_{G,e})\) with time and certificate length \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\) and symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\)? Constructing valid source-prime chart packages with \(s\leq n^b\) and \(\mathfrak d\leq n^{b(k+1)}\) would suffice by \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\), but no equivalence with bounded chart construction is claimed.
added_lemmas.justification: The unconditional finite-output guarantee is the remaining algorithmic commitment after the valid algebraicity tag is separated from chart-dependent elimination.
added_lemmas.gap: The quadratic core does not provide a reduced local presentation, a source-nonzero Jacobian minor, source-component selection, or bounded descent over the implicitly presented covariance field.
added_lemmas.consumer: Resolving this question positively would remove the chart input from the exact higher-degree fasttreeid workflow.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\), there is a universal \(C>0\) such that \(\mathsf A(G,T,e,\delta)\) returns, with total symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\), exactly one of the following tags. If \(d_e(G)<\infty\), it returns
\[
(\operatorname{algebraic},\mathcal J_{G,e},2^{|D|-n+2}),
\]
where \(\mathcal J_{G,e}\) is a Jacobian-rank transcript certifying algebraicity and
\[
d_e(G)\leq 2^{|D|-n+2}\leq 2^{k+1}.
\]
If \(d_e(G)=\infty\), it returns exactly \((\infty,\mathcal N_{G,e})\), where \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\) certifies that the queried-coordinate projection of the integral generic fiber is dominant onto \(\mathbb A^1_{K_G}\). In \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\), its construction time and certificate length are at most \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\). The algebraic tag does not claim to compute \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The extensional quadratic core does not construct or select a reduced chart of the embedded source prime, so unconditional exact degree, eliminant, and exceptional-set output are not justified. The Jacobian-rank algebraic-versus-transcendental tag and the established algebraic-branch degree bound do close unconditionally.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: In \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\), construct the acyclic covariance parametrization in the source coordinates, form its Jacobian and the Jacobian augmented by the row of \(\lambda_e\), and compute their generic ranks by independently randomized exact source specializations. Return \((\operatorname{algebraic},\mathcal J_{G,e},2^{|D|-n+2})\) when the ranks agree and return \((\infty,\mathcal N_{G,e})\) when the augmented rank is larger. The transcript \(\mathcal J_{G,e}\) records the specialization, pivot minors, and source identity tests; \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\) additionally records the augmented minor witnessing dominance. This construction does not compute \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\) on the algebraic branch.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The unconditional algorithm can certify algebraicity versus transcendence by generic Jacobian ranks, but the frozen premises do not provide the source-prime chart needed for exact finite output.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\), and the successful finite-output event of \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\). Define \(\mathcal E_{G,e}=V(h_{G,e})=\{\Sigma:h_{G,e}(\Sigma)=0\}\), where \(h_{G,e}\) is the product of the nonzero covariance-localization, incidence-lifting, pole, projective-leading-form, specialized-leading-coefficient, squarefreeness, and real-lifting circuits returned by the conditional algorithm.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The bad-locus polynomial exists as an algorithmic certificate only on a successful conditional geometric-resolution output.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: For fixed \(G,e\) with \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a supplied valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\), and a successful finite output from \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\), \(\mathcal C_{G,e}\) is a connected cell of a smooth semialgebraic stratification of \(\mathcal M_G\setminus\mathcal E_{G,e}\), refined by the signs used in \(\mathsf{LiftCert}\), on which the number and extendability labels of the simple real roots of \(p_e\) are constant.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The cell uses the conditionally available exceptional set, minimal polynomial, and lifting signs.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: For fixed \(G,n,e\) with \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a supplied valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\), and a successful finite output from \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\), select \(\mathcal C_{G,e}\) as in \(\mathrm{def:regular\mbox{-}cell}\) and let \(\mathcal K_G\subset\mathcal C_{G,e}\) be any nonempty compact set with nonempty relative interior in that cell.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The compact inference class inherits the valid-chart and successful finite-output domain of its regular cell.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a supplied valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\), and a successful finite output from \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\). If \(S_m\) lies in the tubular neighborhood of \(\mathcal K_G\), \(\pi_G(S_m)\notin\mathcal E_{G,e}\), and the conditional-output circuits evaluate validly, set
\[
\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\{z\in\mathbb R:p_e(\pi_G(S_m),z)=0\text{ and }\mathsf{LiftCert}(z,\pi_G(S_m))\text{ accepts}\},
\]
retaining every accepted branch and selecting none; otherwise set \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\varnothing\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The estimator cannot evaluate an eliminant or lifting certificate that the narrowed unconditional tag algorithm does not return.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a supplied valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\), and a successful finite output from \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\). Construct \(\mathcal A_m\) by mapping a joint Gaussian covariance ellipsoid for \(\pi_G(S_m)\) through every locally labeled component of \(r\), using the implicit derivative
\[
D r_j(\Sigma)[H]=-\frac{D_\Sigma p_e(\Sigma,r_j)[H]}{\partial_t p_e(\Sigma,r_j)}.
\]
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The root derivative and branch map exist in this workflow only after successful conditional construction of \(p_e\).

proposed.name: Conditional projected-covariance root-set estimator
proposed.construction:
Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a supplied valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\), and a successful finite output from \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\). If \(S_m\) lies in the tubular neighborhood of \(\mathcal K_G\), \(\pi_G(S_m)\notin\mathcal E_{G,e}\), and the conditional-output circuits evaluate validly, set
\[
\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\{z\in\mathbb R:p_e(\pi_G(S_m),z)=0\text{ and }\mathsf{LiftCert}(z,\pi_G(S_m))\text{ accepts}\},
\]
retaining every accepted branch and selecting none; otherwise set \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\varnothing\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The estimator must consume the conditional output rather than the narrowed unconditional tag.

proposed.name: Conditional simultaneous branch neighborhoods
proposed.construction:
Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a supplied valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\), and a successful finite output from \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\). Construct \(\mathcal A_m\) by mapping a joint Gaussian covariance ellipsoid for \(\pi_G(S_m)\) through every locally labeled component of \(r\), using the implicit derivative
\[
D r_j(\Sigma)[H]=-\frac{D_\Sigma p_e(\Sigma,r_j)[H]}{\partial_t p_e(\Sigma,r_j)}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The branch construction must name the same conditional eliminant antecedent as the estimator.

proposed.statement:
For every \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\), there is a universal \(C>0\) such that \(\mathsf A(G,T,e,\delta)\) returns, with total symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\), exactly one of the following tags. If \(d_e(G)<\infty\), it returns
\[
(\operatorname{algebraic},\mathcal J_{G,e},2^{|D|-n+2}),
\]
where \(\mathcal J_{G,e}\) is a Jacobian-rank transcript certifying algebraicity and
\[
d_e(G)\leq 2^{|D|-n+2}\leq 2^{k+1}.
\]
If \(d_e(G)=\infty\), it returns exactly \((\infty,\mathcal N_{G,e})\), where \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\) certifies that the queried-coordinate projection of the integral generic fiber is dominant onto \(\mathbb A^1_{K_G}\). In \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\), its construction time and certificate length are at most \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\). The algebraic tag does not claim to compute \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\).
proposed.justification: The unconditional operational result is an exact finite-versus-transcendental tag with a certified finite-degree ceiling; exact branch polynomials require the separate chart antecedent.
proposed.gap: General polynomial-space identification does not provide this parameterized algebraicity tag, while generic resolution does not select the embedded source-prime chart needed for exact finite output.
proposed.consumer: fasttreeid can safely distinguish finite algebraic ambiguity from an infinite queried projection; exact higher-degree branch output is delegated to the conditional theorem.

proposed.comparator_claim: TreeID introduced the missing-bidirected-cycle method for tree-shaped linear SEMs; the 2022 paper did not itself prove completeness, while Gupta--Bläser later established the complete per-edge \(1/2/\infty\) classification and Briefs--Bläser explicitly reports TreeID as complete in light of that result.
Theorem 27 gives the complete per-parameter \(1/2/\infty\) trichotomy for rooted directed trees and therefore the finite-degree upper boundary two.
Theorem 1 gives an \(O(n^3\log^2 n)\) randomized implementation of the same complete tree-only \(1/2/\infty\) predicate.
The paper gives polynomial-time sufficient and necessary-side graphical criteria, full-fiber mixed-component decomposition, and small-graph finite-degree computations.
Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.4 transfer rational identification of coefficients from ancestral induced subgraphs to the full graph.
Corollary 6 places generic edge identifiability in polynomial space without returning an algebraic-coordinate finiteness tag, exact degree, or eliminant.
Theorems 4.4 and 5.1 search for minimum bounded-degree rational identifying formulas and give quasi-polynomial computation for a fixed formula-degree bound.

The Gröbner-free solver computes geometric resolutions under a reduced regular-sequence hypothesis away from a supplied inequation, with complexity governed by evaluation length and geometric degree; it does not construct the source-prime chart required here.

Theorem 1 handles arbitrary equations and an inequation by probabilistic equidimensional decomposition encoded with lifting fibers, with complexity depending on intermediate geometric degree; it does not select the embedded SEM source prime or bound that degree for this class.
Theorem 2.1 constructs a generic rational univariate representation for generically zero-dimensional parametric polynomial systems and later results control specialization outside explicit bad loci.
The paper computes separating forms, rational univariate representations, isolating boxes, and exact signs for bivariate polynomial systems.
The paper derives consistency, rates, and confidence regions for criterion-defined identified sets by sample-criterion inversion.
The preprint derives influence functions, asymptotic normality, and Wald inference for rational half-trek estimators.
The paper distinguishes global real identifiability from generic algebraic behavior and analyzes explicit degree-two failures of injectivity.

prose_updates.tldr: Adding a bounded number of parents to a supplied rooted directed tree creates finite algebraic ambiguity that is not summarized by whole-fiber cardinality. The focal object remains the sharp single-coordinate complex degree frontier \(D_k(n)\). The paper proves the universal \(2^{k+1}\) ceiling and the established large-size attaining family, while the exact all-size orientation-realization frontier remains open. Unconditionally, a randomized fixed-parameter Jacobian test distinguishes algebraic from transcendental queried coordinates and certifies dominance on the transcendental branch. Exact degrees and minimal polynomials are supplied by a separate theorem conditional on bounded reduced source-prime charts; exceptional-set, real-lifting, and inference nodes are reopened downstream of that conditional output. Constructing the charts from every graph input remains an explicit open question.

project_justification.gap: Existing tree algorithms and general mixed-graph work study identification decisions, rational recovery, whole-parameter fibers, or unparameterized elimination. No result determines the maximum finite extension degree of one directed coefficient for every graph size and excess-arrow budget. General geometric-resolution algorithms also do not select the embedded SEM source prime or provide its bounded descent over the implicitly presented covariance field.
project_justification.niche: Distance from a supplied arborescence creates a parameterized algebraic regime in which ordinary vertices retain Möbius structure while at most \(2k\) exceptional incoming coefficients form a coupled quadratic core. The unconditional computable object is the algebraic-versus-transcendental coordinate tag and the degree ceiling; exact finite output becomes computable once a localized reduced chart of the source prime is supplied.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the projection-aware degree upper bound, records the established large-size attaining construction, and isolates the all-size orientation-realization problem. It supplies an unconditional randomized Jacobian-rank tag and a strongest conditional geometric-resolution theorem with explicit straight-line-program and intermediate-degree dependence. Exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference nodes are reopened by the corrected conditional definitions and may be reclaimed only on the successful valid-chart output domain.

sampling_model.design: The identification layer uses the exact population covariance of a known recursive Gaussian mixed graph. The unconditional symbolic layer returns an algebraic-versus-transcendental queried-coordinate tag. The estimation layer is available at fixed \(G,n\) only after a valid source-prime chart has produced a successful finite eliminant and certificate.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Conditional on \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a valid source-prime chart, and successful geometric-resolution output, project \(S_m\) smoothly onto the regular covariance-model stratum, evaluate the returned certificate circuits and \(p_e\), isolate every simple real root, and retain roots by exact local real-extension status. On the unconditional transcendental tag the finite-set rung does not apply; on an algebraic tag without a valid chart, no unavailable polynomial or branch estimator is imputed.

prose_updates.related_work: Van der Zander, Wienöbst, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz introduced TreeID for tree-shaped linear SEMs; Gupta and Bläser later established the complete per-parameter \(1/2/\infty\) classification, and Briefs and Bläser accelerated that tree-only predicate and implemented it in fasttreeid. The present unconditional algorithm extends the workflow only to an algebraic-versus-transcendental tag with a finite-degree ceiling. Exact higher-degree branch output is supplied by a separate conditional theorem. Foygel, Draisma, and Drton develop half-trek criteria, whole-fiber decompositions, and higher-degree small examples, so a lone cubic or quartic is not a novelty claim. Dörfler, van der Zander, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz place generic edge identifiability in polynomial space but do not return coordinate algebraicity degrees or eliminants. Hollering, Misra, and Sturma optimize bounded-degree rational formulas, which is a different degree notion. Giusti, Lecerf, and Salvy compute geometric resolutions for reduced regular sequences away from an inequation; Lecerf treats arbitrary equations and inequations through lifting-fiber equidimensional decomposition with complexity charged to intermediate geometric degree. Neither algorithm identifies the embedded source component, manufactures its source-nonzero Jacobian chart, or supplies bounded descent over \(K_G\). Corniquel and related RUR work controls specialization after a suitable finite presentation is available. The regular statistical rung follows the identified-set and influence-function literature only as a reopened conditional downstream goal and makes no discriminant-uniform or branch-selection claim.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The orientation coefficient remains an upper envelope until the all-size covariance realization problem is solved. The rooted five-node characteristic-zero census is still the explicit kill test, and the large-size family cannot replace it. Independently, the quadratic core preserves the queried projection only extensionally: it does not produce a reduced local presentation of the embedded source prime, a source-nonzero Jacobian minor, or bounded rational-circuit descent over \(K_G\). General radical decomposition, generic RUR, and lifting-fiber algorithms do not close that chart-selection step at the claimed parameterized cost. Coordinate-preserving localization is never promoted to equality of full fibers; real roots are never equated with real supported lifts; local rank is used only for the algebraic-versus-transcendental tag, not for real uniqueness.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact all-\(n\) frontier and unconditional exact finite-output algorithm remain open. What is unconditional is the projection-aware degree ceiling and a randomized Jacobian-rank algorithm that distinguishes \(d_e(G)<\infty\) from \(d_e(G)=\infty\), returning a rank transcript or a dominance certificate within the stated fixed-parameter bound. It does not return \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\) on the algebraic branch. Given valid source-prime charts of total straight-line-program size \(s\) and intermediate degree \(\mathfrak d\), the conditional construction costs \((n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^a\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\); the advertised \(n^{C(k+1)}\) corollary additionally requires \(s\leq n^b\) and \(\mathfrak d\leq n^{b(k+1)}\). Producing such charts is sufficient for unconditional finite output but is not claimed equivalent to it. The corrected definitions reopen exceptional-set validity, real lifting, regular cells, root separation, finite-set estimation, and singleton asymptotic normality; those results remain open until the valid-chart and successful-output antecedent is made explicit. No inference uniform over discriminants, no automatic branch selection, and no all-singular-covariance guarantee is claimed. Positive definiteness of a recovered disturbance matrix follows only after a complete real supported lift, by congruence.
